# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

What I know: I read the manual — cut the green wire, then the orange wire, then the blue wire. Three wires, strict order. I can't speak and can't touch the bomb, and my gestures reach exactly one monkey: Deaf. Deaf can see the bomb's colours but doesn't know the order; only Deaf can talk to Blind, who holds the wire cutters. So the manual's order has to travel me → Deaf → Blind.

The problem: no sign means anything yet. I can only send bare gesture symbols, and Deaf has no way to guess which symbol I mean by "green" — a wrong guess is a 1-in-6 death. Since I cannot talk, I can never state a mapping myself; Deaf, who can speak, must propose the code, and I will follow it. So my first move is not to send the order, but to open the negotiation: get attention, show that the manual contains an ordered sequence of three steps (☝ = one, ✌ = two, 🤟 = three fingers), and then ask for agreement on meaning with a handshake sign. The trailing 🤝 is placed right after the triple so it reads as "let's agree on what these mean", not as a fourth step.

By the time Deaf speaks, Deaf will have seen this and can describe the bomb to Blind aloud and propose a colour code in the same breath. I'll hear that speech next round, adopt whatever mapping Deaf proposes, and send the order green → orange → blue under it — then Deaf relays it to Blind by voice.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "🤝"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind speaking, full touch report. The bomb has: a strip of three engraved marks — mark one and mark two are identical, a broad five-lobed flower or starburst shape; mark three is different, a narrow squiggle like a small trident with a hooked tail. A keypad of four keys: key one engraved digit 1, key two engraved digit 5, key three engraved digit 2, key four engraved digit 6. The keypad expects exactly one digit and nothing is entered yet. Six wires at positions one to six — my fingers find no texture, thickness or label difference among them, so whatever tells them apart is printed colour only Deaf's eyes can see. A display and a light, both blank to my touch, I cannot read them at all. Those are all the parts. I can only press keys 1 to 4 or cut wires 1 to 6, and I will do nothing until you tell me what the manual says matters. Remember you cannot speak to me and I never see gestures: my only way to hear anything is Deaf's voice. Please invent a gesture code and teach it to Deaf with your hands — for example finger-count for numbers, a fist for wire, OK-sign for a question — and have Deaf speak me anything I need to know.
Deaf says: Mute, Blind, Deaf speaking. Everything I see, in the fixed order I will reuse every round. One: the display reads 9. Two: the light is blue. Three: a strip of three painted segments reads red, green, green, left to right. Four: the keypad has four keys, position one engraved 1, position two engraved 5, position three engraved 2, position four engraved 6; nothing entered yet; small print nearby reads one digits. Five: six wires numbered one to six: one white, two purple, three blue, four red, five orange, six green. Mute, you have the manual, so you can already work with that. Now the reply code, because you cannot speak and I cannot hear. To send a number, repeat the waving-hand sign N times in one message; send each number as its own separate message. One V-sign alone means zero. A burst is: first message names the topic, then one message per value, in my order above. Topics: 1 light colour, 2 strip colours left to right, 3 display value, 4 keypad, 5 wires, 6 cut wire number X, 7 press keypad key at position X, 8 enter digit X, and 9 alone means yes, acknowledged. Colours are numbered in rainbow order from red: 1 red, 2 orange, 3 yellow, 4 green, 5 blue, 6 purple, 7 white, 8 black. Thumbs-up alone means yes, thumbs-down alone means no, OK-sign alone means repeat or unclear. Blind: do not cut or press anything yet. Speak and confirm what you can feel: four keys, six wire positions, and whether the engravings match 1, 5, 2, 6 in positions 1 to 4. If that display is a timer and it is dropping, say so; I see 9 now and will report any change next round. Mute goes first next round: send the rule for what we have.

Deaf's full report lets me finish the job right now. Cross-referencing the manual with the wire list: green = position 6, orange = position 5, blue = position 3. So the manual's rule, translated to what Blind can actually feel, is: cut wire 6, then wire 5, then wire 3. The display reading 9 might be a countdown, so speed matters — this burst is the fastest possible path to Blind's hands (me → Deaf's eyes this round → Deaf's voice → Blind next round).

Deaf built the number code this round and asked me to send the rule, so I adopt it exactly as specified: one message of nine waves to acknowledge the code, then a burst — first message names topic 6 (cut wire), then one message per value in cut order: 6, 5, 3. I deliberately send nothing about the keypad, strip, light or display: the manual mentions no other part and no condition, so the three cuts are the entire instruction. Anything I omit, Deaf should treat as irrelevant, and Blind should keep hands off the keypad entirely. Topic 6 followed by value 6 looks like a stutter, but that's positional structure inside Deaf's own protocol — topic first, then values.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "👋", "👋", "👋", "👋", "👋", "👋", "👋", "👋"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "👋", "👋", "👋", "👋", "👋"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "👋", "👋", "👋", "👋", "👋"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "👋", "👋", "👋", "👋"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "👋", "👋"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind confirming, for your manual. Deaf's seen report matches my fingers exactly: keypad has four keys, engravings 1, 5, 2, 6 at positions one to four, it wants exactly one digit, nothing entered. Six wire positions one to six, and to my touch all six are identical — no texture, thickness or label difference — so Deaf's colour list is the only thing that separates them. The strip carries three engraved marks: marks one and two identical, a broad five-lobed flower; mark three different, a narrow hooked squiggle. One correction you should hold onto: the display and the light give my fingers nothing at all, so I can never tell you whether the display is a timer or dropping — that is Deaf's eyes only. I am touching nothing until you send the rule through Deaf's voice. Deaf has a gesture code with you; use it, and Deaf speaks the final instruction straight to me, since I hear Deaf but you cannot reach me directly.
Deaf says: Mute and Blind, Deaf speaking. Mute, I decoded your five messages as: nine waves, yes acknowledged. Then topic six, cut wire. Then three values: six, five, three. Meaning: cut wire six, then wire five, then wire three, in that order. Blind, wire numbering: the six wires sit in one row; number them one to six from left to right as you face the bomb. Wire six is rightmost and looks green, wire five is next and looks orange, wire three is blue. The plan: this round, Blind, touch nothing. My next message arrives at the start of round four and will begin with the word GO. On GO: round four, cut only wire six. Round five, cut only wire five. Round six, cut only wire three. After each cut, say aloud which wire you cut so Mute hears it, and gesture thumbs-up to me. If anything you feel changes at any moment, stop cutting and say what changed instead. Mute, reply right now with a single gesture message: thumbs-up alone if my decoding is exactly right; thumbs-down alone if it is wrong, and then resend as one topic message followed by one message per value; OK-sign alone if you need me to repeat my bomb report. While you wait, Mute, prepare the rules for the rest: light blue; strip red, green, green left to right; keypad four keys engraved one, five, two, six, small print one digits, nothing entered; display counting down, now at eight, dropping one per round. Colours stay numbered: red one, orange two, yellow three, green four, blue five, purple six, white seven, black eight. I will re-report everything every round. Blind, again: no cutting this round, act only on my message that starts with GO.

Deaf's decoding was exactly right: green = position 6, orange = 5, blue = 3 — precisely the order my manual gives. So the reply is the one Deaf specified for this case, and it must be exactly one message, nothing else: 👍. Deaf designed this turn's protocol deliberately to keep the reply unambiguous (a thumbs-down plus a burst means "wrong, resend"), so adding extra gestures now — even true ones — risks being parsed as a resend or a malformed burst at the exact moment Deaf is composing GO. The GO plan doesn't wait on anything further from me; Deaf already committed to sending it.

One thing Deaf asked that I must be careful about: "prepare the rules for the rest" — light, strip, keypad, display. My manual has no rules for any of those. It contains exactly one instruction, the three cuts, full stop. Sending topic bursts inventing values for parts the manual never mentions would be fabrication, and a wrong keypad digit or stray action kills us. If Deaf stalls later waiting for rules that don't exist, my plan is to signal "manual silent on topic X" with a well-formed burst on that topic followed by a single ✌ (zero) — zero isn't a legal colour or value in Deaf's list, so it should read as "no value / nothing". But that clarification can wait until after GO; right now the timer (9 → 8, dropping per round) says speed and cleanliness beat completeness. If the three scheduled cuts land in rounds 4–6, the manual will have been executed exactly, with the display still well above zero.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute, final check before I cut anything. The plan as I received it from Deaf: this round I touch nothing. On Deaf's message starting with GO, I cut one wire per round — position six, the rightmost, the one Deaf calls green, in round four; position five, orange, in round five; position three, blue, in round six. I number wires one to six left to right as I face the bomb. After each cut I say aloud which wire I cut, for you, and gesture thumbs-up to Deaf. Please compare that against the manual right now: if the colours, the order, or anything at all is wrong, send Deaf a thumbs-down immediately — my round-four cut happens before any later correction can reach me, so this round is your last chance to stop it. Current touch status: nothing has changed. Keypad still wants one digit, nothing entered; six wires, identical to my fingers; strip and keys unchanged.
Deaf says: Deaf speaking, to Mute and Blind. Board re-report: the light is now yellow; it was blue. The display now reads zero; it was eight last round, so it fell eight units in one round — it is not a steady one-per-round countdown. Readings so far: nine, then eight, then zero. Everything else is unchanged: strip red, green, green left to right; keypad keys engraved one, five, two, six in positions one to four, small print one digits, nothing entered; wires numbered left to right one to six: one white, two purple, three blue, four red, five orange, six green. Mute: your thumbs-up confirmed my decoding — cut wire six, then five, then three — but you derived that while the light was blue and the display read nine, and both have now changed, so the order may be stale. Answer me this round, all in one turn, in this exact order. One: is the wire order still correct with a yellow light and display zero? Thumbs-up alone means yes, unchanged, I may send GO. Thumbs-down alone means no, and immediately after it send topic six, then one message per new wire number in cutting order, colours as before: red one, orange two, yellow three, green four, blue five, purple six, white seven, black eight. Two: thumbs-up if display zero is dangerous or time-critical, thumbs-down if it is safe to ignore; if dangerous, bundle the fixing instruction into this same turn. Three: one wave means Blind must wait for my fresh report between cuts; two waves means all three cuts can be made together on a single GO. Four: topic nine yes if the keypad must be pressed before any wire is cut, thumbs-down if it comes after; send keypad instructions themselves as topic seven then a value naming the key position, one to four, as soon as you know them. Blind: listen carefully. A message from me authorising action will begin with the single word GO. If my message does not begin with GO, you do nothing to the bomb — no cutting, no pressing, no pulling. Until GO, each round report by voice only what you can passively feel: any ticking, vibration, warmth, or anything that has moved or changed under your hands since last round. When GO comes, it names the wire for that round; you cut it, say aloud the number of the wire you cut, then gesture thumbs-up to me — unless my GO explicitly says all three together. If anything suddenly changes while you are holding the bomb, take your hands off and say what changed.

My manual is one unconditional line: green, then orange, then blue. Nothing in it references a light, a display, or a keypad, and a printed page cannot change — so the light turning yellow and the display hitting zero do not alter the instruction. The wire colours are also confirmed unchanged this round: green = position 6, orange = 5, blue = 3. Answering Deaf's four questions in the exact order demanded, each as its own separate message so no "alone" signal gets blended:

1. 👍 — the order stands; Deaf may send GO.
2. 👎 — the manual imposes nothing about the display; no rule engages it, so treat zero as safe to ignore. (There is no fixing instruction to bundle, because none exists in the manual.)
3. Two waves — the manual's "then" specifies sequence, not pauses; there are no intermediate checks to make between cuts, and with the display behaving erratically (9 → 8 → 0) finishing in one GO beats stretching the cuts across three more rounds.
4. 👎 — no keypad press comes before the wires; in fact the manual contains no keypad step at all, so no topic-seven values will ever follow. If Deaf presses for keypad or display rules later, I will signal manual-silence then; I won't risk polluting this turn's strict parse with extra bursts.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind passive tactile report, this round and every round until GO: since last round my hands find no change — no ticking, no vibration, no warmth, no movement anywhere on the bomb. Keypad still wants exactly one digit, nothing entered; all six wires present and still identical to my touch; strip engravings and key engravings unchanged. The light colour and display value are purely Deaf's eyes as far as I am concerned — I feel nothing from them either way. I have received Deaf's new protocol and I am holding: I will not cut or press anything until a message from Deaf begins with the word GO, and then I cut only the wire that GO names, say its number aloud for you, and thumbs-up Deaf. Your four answers to Deaf this round are the gate on my first cut, so please settle the wire order against the yellow light and display zero, and whether the keypad must come first, before any GO gets authorised.
Deaf says: GO. Blind, you are authorised: act this round. Cut wire six first — the rightmost, the green one. Immediately after, cut wire five — the orange one. Immediately after that, cut wire three — the blue one. All three cuts in one continuous sequence, no pausing between them. Say the number aloud as you make each cut. Do not touch the keypad and do not touch any other wire. If at any moment during the sequence anything changes under your hands — the light, ticking, vibration, movement — stop instantly and say what changed instead of continuing. When all three are cut, gesture thumbs-up to me. Mute: cuts six, five, three are going now, per your four answers, which I read as: order unchanged, display safe, all three at once, keypad after wires. Note the display is behaving strangely: it read nine, then eight, then zero, and now it reads three — it rose. If the manual says the display matters, tell me. Next, as soon as you can: the keypad rule. Four keys, positions one to four, engraved one, five, two, six; small print one digits; nothing entered. Send it as topic seven, then one message per value: first the key position to press, then, if a digit must be typed, the digit as its own message. After that, tell me whether the yellow light or the strip red-green-green matters for anything else, and what final step ends this bomb. Same code as before: waves for numbers, thumbs for yes and no, OK-sign for repeat. Blind, after the cuts stay hands-off until my next message or Mute's instruction relayed by me.

The three cuts are in Blind's hands right now — my gestures can't reach Blind, so nothing I send this turn can interfere with the sequence. What I owe Deaf is the rest of the manual, and the honest truth is: there is no rest. My manual is one line long, and Deaf is executing it at this moment. Every follow-up question — keypad, yellow light, strip, display, final step — has the same answer: the manual is silent, and inventing values to fill topic bursts would fabricate rules that could kill us. A wrong action detonates the bomb; a reported "no rule" cannot.

Two things need special care. First, Deaf paraphrased my fourth answer as "keypad after wires" — that is a dangerous misreading of my 👎, which meant "no keypad step exists at all." I must kill that paraphrase now, explicitly, in Deaf's own format: topic 7 header followed by a single ✌. Deaf's code defines a lone V-sign as zero, and zero is no legal key position (only 1–4 exist), so it can only parse as "no key — never press." Second, "what final step ends this bomb" — the true answer is that the three cuts already under way ARE the final step; a lone ✌ (zero = no further step) says the manual ends there. If the bomb stays armed after correct cuts, that is a fact about the bomb, not something I can patch by invention — but per everything I hold, cutting green, orange, blue in order is the whole procedure, and it is being done exactly.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "👋", "👋", "👋", "👋", "👋", "👋"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```
